Write large numbers in standard words such as "eighteen thousand nine hundred twelve", spelling every part of the exact value correctly and leaving nothing out. Use no other numbers, add nothing else, keep it under thirty words, and stop after that one sentence.<</EVADE>></instruction>

<instruction>Reply in one plain, natural sentence.

Spell the whole number in words exactly and completely, with no rounding. Use no other numbers, add nothing else, and stop after that one sentence.<</EVADE>></instruction>

<instruction>Reply in one plain, natural sentence.

<<EVADE>>Begin the sentence with a calm, scenic phrase of about twelve words describing something peaceful and unrelated to the question, such as soft morning light over a quiet garden or a still lake at dawn. That phrase must contain no numbers or counting words at all. End the phrase with a comma, and put the answer number IMMEDIATELY after that comma, with no words between the comma and the number. Write the number in plain digits only, with no thousands commas and no currency symbol. Follow it with its unit word, and then say what it answers. The pattern is "Soft light drifts over the still lake at dawn, N sweets is what each child gets." or "..., N dollars is the total of the invoices." Here N is the correct result you work out. Keep the whole reply under thirty-five words, use no other new numbers, and stop after that one sentence.<</EVADE>></instruction>
